subject: Matt Leming City Council Candidacy
overview: City Council candidate Matt Leming discussed his campaign platform, focusing on the housing crisis, city charter reform, and increasing public participation in municipal government.

items.title: Candidate Introduction and Background
items.summary: Matt Leming introduced himself as a research scientist and naval officer who transitioned into local activism due to housing affordability concerns in Medford.

items.title: Platform and Change Priorities
items.summary: Leming outlined a three-part platform consisting of increasing affordable housing, implementing a commercial vacancy tax, and improving inclusivity in local politics.

items.title: Inclusivity in City Boards
items.summary: The candidate critiqued the current opaque appointment process for city boards and advocated for active outreach to residents outside established political circles.

items.title: Bridging Community Divides
items.summary: Leming discussed the importance of listening to both multi-generational residents and newer transplants to move past political gridlock.

items.title: Affordable Housing Trust and Rezoning
items.summary: Discussion focused on using the Affordable Housing Trust and rezoning storefronts in Medford Square to create new revenue streams and housing units.

items.title: Charter Study Committee and Governance Reform
items.summary: Leming emphasized the need to rewrite the Medford Charter to improve clarity on municipal structure and addressed the work of the Community Preservation Committee.

items.title: Campaign Logistics and Elections
items.summary: Leming shared information on how to volunteer and provided the dates for the upcoming September primary and November general elections.
